messages:
Jon Patel: Heads up — I sketched a canary plan for model upgrade v2.0. Want feedback on percent rungs + safety checks before I wire it into rollout-api.
Maria Chen: Paste the plan? I'm more concerned about the gating rules than the timing.
Jon Patel: Sure. Thinking non-linear rungs: 0 -> 0.5 -> 3 -> 10 -> 30 -> 70 -> 100. Hold durations: 5m, 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h, 2h respectively. Basic checks: p95 latency, error-rate, and a simple semantic-quality regression (eval-set delta).
Sahil Rao: Non-linear looks reasonable. Suggest we add an anomaly-score gate that looks at streaming evals (new behavioral mismatch detector). If anomaly_score > 0.25 at any rung, abort and roll back.
Kevin Park: UX note — console should show "rung health" with small sparkline and a red/amber/green badge per check. Also allow manual advance even if checks are warning.
Maria Chen: Can we add per-route quotas for the early rungs so we avoid noisy clients skewing metrics? e.g., cap any single client to 5% of rung traffic.
Jon Patel: Good call. Also want to ensure cross-region fallbacks: if region A is failing, we should automatically reduce that region's weight and shift to region B model variant.
Sahil Rao: For metrics, let's gate on the following: latency_p95 increase > 15% over baseline, error_rate > 0.8% absolute, anomaly_score > 0.25, hallucination_ratio delta > 2% (on a small prompt set). All checks run in rolling 5m windows with 95% CI.
Maria Chen: Proposed API payload sketch:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-model-v2",
  "rungs": [
    {"pct": 0.5, "hold": "5m"},
    {"pct": 3,   "hold": "10m"},
    {"pct": 10,  "hold": "20m"},
    {"pct": 30,  "hold": "30m"},
    {"pct": 70,  "hold": "1h"},
    {"pct": 100, "hold": "2h"}
  ],
  "checks": [
    {"metric": "latency_p95", "type": "relative", "threshold": 0.15},
    {"metric": "error_rate", "type": "absolute", "threshold": 0.008},
    {"metric": "anomaly_score", "type": "absolute", "threshold": 0.25}
  ],
  "client_quota": {"per_client_pct_max": 5}
}
```
Kevin Park: API shape looks fine. Minor suggestion: add an optional `manual_override` boolean and `auto_rollforward_on_pass` flag. Defaults: auto true for small tests, false for enterprise customers.
Jon Patel: What about A/B style cohorts? I want to support deterministic cohort keys so product experiments can run alongside canaries.
Sahil Rao: We can treat cohorts as named slices. Rollout engine should accept `cohort_weights` map. Important: checks must be computed per-cohort and aggregated — abort if any cohort fails its thresholds.
Maria Chen: Operationally: also add a soft-sla guard — if routing queue depth > X, throttle canary growth by an attenuation factor. We had bad incidents where canaries amplified backpressure.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout-id=rr-2024-04-01-331, model=redwood-model-v2, initial-rung=0.5% :rocket:
Jon Patel: :eyes: I'll hook my dashboard to the rollout-id and watch the rung pass/fail signals.
Kevin Park: I'll add the small UI tile for rung health and a manual "advance" button. UX will show why a rung failed (metric + current value + threshold).
Maria Chen: OK let's iterate on this config: Jon will update the PR with the API changes, Sahil will wire anomaly detection hooks, Kevin will mock the UI. Ping here when PR is up.
Sahil Rao: SGTM. One more: include an emergency "panic" policy in API that immediately pins traffic to previous model and notifies oncall. Something like `on_abort: { action: "pin_previous", notify: ["#oncall"] }`.
Jon Patel: Agreed. I'll add `on_abort` and include a small e2e test in rollout-api that simulates a sudden spike in error_rate.
Maria Chen: Sweet. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
